partition_policy.training: all target facts except source-exclusive validation and blind facts

results.name: Disease-caused process suppression
results.hypothesis: A drug may treat a disease by decreasing a biological process that the disease itself causes.
results.body: SemMedDB disease causes process; CTD drug decreases the same process
results.mechanism_rationale: The rule directly composes a disease-to-process causal claim with an opposing signed drug effect, but the process is downstream of disease rather than proven etiologic.
results.trapi_notes: The two positive edges and direction qualifier are TRAPI-expressible; source restrictions and disease ontology constraints require post-processing.
results.cypher:
MATCH (object:Disease)-[etiology:CAUSES]->(process:BiologicalProcess)
MATCH (subject:Drug)-[effect:AFFECTS]->(process)
WHERE effect.qualified_predicate = 'biolink:causes'
  AND effect.object_direction_qualifier = 'decreased'
  AND 'infores:ctd' IN
      coalesce(effect.primary_knowledge_sources, [])
  AND 'infores:semmeddb' IN
      coalesce(etiology.primary_knowledge_sources, [])
  AND coalesce(object._miner_disease_descendant_degree, 0) <= 500
  AND object._miner_disease_superclass_degree >= 1
  AND object.id STARTS WITH 'MONDO:'
RETURN DISTINCT subject.id AS subject_id, object.id AS object_id

results.name: Disease-caused process activation control
results.hypothesis: Increasing a process caused by the disease is a matched worsening control for downstream process suppression.
results.body: R443 with increased rather than decreased process effect
results.mechanism_rationale: The same disease-process architecture is retained while the drug reinforces rather than suppresses the downstream process.

results.body: SemMedDB process causes disease; CTD drug decreases the same process
results.mechanism_rationale: The rule opposes a signed drug effect to an explicitly etiologic process-to-disease edge without requiring a gene intermediary.
